name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
explanation: This is the stricter version of SC 2.4.11: at this AAA level, no part of a focused element can be hidden by other content the page created, not even partially. Where the Level AA criterion only requires that some part of the focused element stays visible, this criterion requires the entire focused element to remain fully visible and unobstructed, with nothing overlapping any part of it.
whoItAffects: Keyboard-only users benefit further here because even a partially obscured focused element, allowed under the Level AA criterion, can make it hard to read a full label, understand a control's current state, or interact with it confidently if part of it is cut off or covered. This matters especially for elements with meaningful content extending across their full width or height, like a focused table row or a wide button with descriptive text, where losing even an edge could hide relevant information.
howToTest: Tab through the page near any fixed or sticky elements, headers, footers, banners, or floating widgets, and examine each focused element closely rather than just checking that some part of it is visible. If any pixel of a focused element is covered by overlapping page content, even a small sliver at one edge, this stricter AAA criterion fails, even in cases where the Level AA minimum would still pass.

check.question: As a user tabs through a page, a focused button is 95% visible but its bottom two pixels are covered by a sticky footer bar. This already passes the Level AA SC 2.4.11 since most of the button is visible. Does it also pass the stricter SC 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)?
choices: Yes, because passing SC 2.4.11 automatically satisfies SC 2.4.12
No, because SC 2.4.12 requires no part of the focused component to be hidden, and even two pixels being covered fails that
Yes, because 95% visibility is well above any reasonable threshold
It depends only on whether the button is a submit button
